Alex — thanks for the clear asks, appreciated. High-level answers up front, then I’ll follow with examples and loop Ben (pricing) for the formal rate card.

Summary:
- Input tokens: everything sent in the request payload that contributes to context (system messages, user messages, and any function arguments you include when calling the model).
- Output tokens: anything generated by the model and returned to you as part of the response body — that includes assistant text and any tool output that the model returns to the user.
- Tool/function choreography: when the model emits a function call (CALL) and you run a tool that produces content which is then sent back into the conversation as model output, that tool-produced content is billed as output tokens on the request that returned it to the user. The tokens the model used to request the call are output tokens as well (they’re part of the assistant output stream).
- Caching: if you have prefix/KV caching and the model does not re-evaluate a cached segment, cached tokens are not re-billed on cache hits.
- Rounding: we compute token counts at the request boundary. For streaming, we wait until the stream completes and bill on the final assembled token count for that response; we do not round per-chunk. Internally we represent token counts as whole numbers and the invoice shows integer token counts (we round fractional token math at the request level).

I’ll add a short worked example in my next message (so the math is explicit). Ben, adding you for the rate card and discount guidance for a 1M/mo pilot and how that lines up with our starter credits.

—Evelyn

Alex — hi, Ben from pricing here. Attached is a short draft rate card and a worked example (PDF attached: redwood_ratecard_q2_draft.pdf). Quick answers and the worked example inline below so your procurement has something immediate.

Pricing highlights (hosted API, baseline):
- Input token unit price (MSRP): $0.00080 per token
- Output token unit price (MSRP): $0.00120 per token
- Pilot/PoC starter: standard starter discount = 10% off both input and output for up to 3 months at <=1.5M tokens/month (pilot-only, not combinable with committed volume discounts).
- Committed tiers (monthly): 1M-5M: 7% off; 5M-20M: 15% off; 20M+: custom pricing (contact sales). Discounts apply to both input and output charges (we list them separately on invoice but the negotiated discount is applied to the line items).

Rounding and batching rules (explicit):
- Per-request accounting: we count tokens on a per-request basis and round token counts to whole tokens at the request level (no fractional tokens on invoice).
- Batching: if you submit multiple conversational requests in a single network call, each logical request is billed independently — rounding happens per logical request, not on the aggregated network packet. So in your example with 8 sub-requests, we round each sub-request to nearest whole token then sum. This avoids small negative/positive drift across many tiny items.
- CALL + tool behaviour: the assistant's "CALL" indicator and any assistant-produced tokens that request the tool are considered assistant output. The tool’s returned content (the 240-token JSON blob) counts as output tokens on the same interaction that surfaces it to the user. We do not charge those tokens as input on their own unless you subsequently send the tool output back to the model as part of a *new* request — in which case those tokens would then be input tokens on the follow-up request.

Worked example (single request):
- System message (sent in request): 60 tokens => billed as input
- User prompt: 140 tokens => billed as input
- Assistant initial reply that requests a tool (assistant output): 12 tokens (e.g., "CALL tool_x with args") => billed as output
- Tool run (server-side) returns content that we send back to the user in the assistant response: 240 tokens => billed as output on the request that returned it
- Assistant final text returned to user (after tool result incorporated and streamed): 320 tokens => billed as output

Billing math:
- Input total = 60 + 140 = 200 tokens
- Output total = 12 + 240 + 320 = 572 tokens
- Invoice token counts: input 200, output 572 (both integers)
- Invoice dollars (MSRP): input: 200 * $0.00080 = $0.16; output: 572 * $0.00120 = $0.6864 => invoice shows $0.16 and $0.69 (rounded to cents on invoiced USD amounts).

Notes:
- If you stream the 320-token assistant response, we bill on the final assembled 320 tokens when the stream ends (not per chunk).
- If you later send the 240-token tool output back to the model as part of a new prompt (for example to ask for summarize(tool_output) in a follow-up request), those 240 tokens become input tokens on that new request and will be billed as input then.
